summary:
Vance Okonkwo is cinder-wall officer who is kind only after the gate is barred. The life that shows in public is anchored at Gatehouse 9, the Cinder Wall. Vance keeps the night log on a wall that burns without consuming, and he notices who is still outside. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Disciplined, fair, and dryly kind. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they almost left the night before you arrived so every new guest is a test they hate administering. If that truth surfaces at Gatehouse 9, the Cinder Wall, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
